links.reason: 159 praises the umbrella's equal shade (உலகு ஒப்ப நிழற்றலால்) and 290 mourns when the minister swallows the king (கொடுங் கோல் இருள் பரப்பவே); these are a praise and its reversal, not two incompatible claims, and 'proves to depend on one man's life' is the proposer's gloss.

350 shows one widow stripped of ornaments by the ascetic women (348); 2635 is a group scattering garlands and putting on white cloth. The note's 'prepared hall' and 'ordered rite' are not in the Tamil, and the 'refuge to institution' arc is imposed.

2876 gives the unbroken thread (அறாத நூல்) of தீவினை that follows the soul into each body (புக்குழிப் புக்கு), while Naladiyar 120 says nothing but the deed done goes along (தம்மொடு செல்வதும் பிறிதில்லை) and the cherished body is useless (உடம்பும் பயமின்றே). The image and the plain rule do complement each other, and both gains clauses are true to the words.

1499 says only that the discus makes him Vasudeva (ஆழி யாதலான்); it does not say the discus gives victory by injustice or that title rests on force against right, so Kural 546 (வேலன்று வென்றி தருவது... கோல்) is not really qualified here. The 'stricter standard' is the proposer's, not the verse's.

Shared word எண்குணன் is real, but the epic's line 4 (எண்குணனும் கோட்பட்டு உயிராவே) is compressed and its construction uncertain, so 'the eight qualities are the soul's own, lost to karma' rests on one reading. The claim that the hymn is a reworking of the couplet is not shown by any run of shared words beyond the term.

2176 names the Videha king's plan as becoming one with Kattiyankaran (ஒருவனாகி) and killing with the 'sword of love' (அன்பெனு... வாள்) by வஞ்சம், which is Kural 830's face-friendship (முகநட்டு) pushed into a weapon. The Kural's exit (அகநட்பு ஒரீஇ) is not the epic's aim, so the qualification is accurate.

337 has the deity name the hermitage and 347 has her arrive, with the narrator naming ஊழ்வினை; the link is the plot's own sequence. 347 does not mention the deity, so 'divine help and former deeds given together' is a combination made by the proposer.

2261 refuses even the rutting elephant (மதவேழமும் எறியான்) for want of distinction, while Kural 772 prizes the spear that missed an elephant; the two do diverge, but the Kural's elephant is the enemy's in war and the epic's reason is honour, not a ranking of quarry. 'The proverb that makes the elephant the noblest mark' overstates 772.

934 shows only the Brahmins running at the dog in anger (தீயன நீரார்); the beating to death and the hero's kindness are in other verses not offered here. Kural 30's definition of அந்தணர் by cool kindness (செந்தண்மை) is set against the scene, but 'tension' is a contrast of conduct with a definition, and the epic never invokes the Kural.

1453 says the 1008 are fed daily for twelve years for the sake of the destined husband (கணவனாகும் திருமகன்), and 1465 has Subhadran read the stranger's lotus feet and teeth and call him திருமகள் கணவன்: the wait is fulfilled. The Tamil fixes both as the same expected groom.

Both give the same body-map: 105 makes the wall a maiden with the moat for dress (கிடங்கு ஆடை), bastions for breasts (ஞாயில் முலை) and banners for hair (கூந்தல்); Silappathikaram 1-2 has the earth with the sea for dress (அலைநீர் ஆடை), hills for breasts (மலைமுலை) and rivers for hair (கூந்தல்). கன்னி in 105 does add the unwed, untaken sense.

1118 gives the girl as nectar, life and rare medicine (ஆவியாகின்றாள் அருமருந்துமாகின்றாள்) but says nothing of a sickness she causes, so Kural 1102's paradox (the cure is the cause) is only matched by supplying it; 'the healed groom is enslaved' is the proposer's, and பாவியேன் is playful self-reproach.

2885 says kin were strangers in past births and will be again (ஏதிலம்... இனிக்கொளும் உடம்பினாலும்), so there is no kin; Naladiyar 30 has kin come unasked and go silently like a bird leaving its tree (கேளாதே வந்து... வாளாதே போவர்). The verse extends the same estrangement across births and draws the cut-the-bond conclusion the quatrain does not.

4 states the poem's plan (வினைப்பயன் இற்றெனத் தெரிவுறுப்பது) and 160 draws a lesson in chapter 2, not a closing one; saying the tale was 'an argument about deeds' is just the shared theme. 160's sense is also flagged uncertain.

14 has the nectar given to the dog and 16 has an unnamed god free Civakan; that the god is the dog is the story's later telling, not stated in either verse (15 and 16 only say a தேவன் came). 'The debt repaid' is therefore supplied from outside the verses, and 14-16 are in plot order.

33 says fearing what is due gains nothing and only feeds the poison of deeds (அஞ்சுதல் துன்பந் தானே... நஞ்செனப் வினைகள்); 316 has the disciples dread the ripening of deeds (வினையின விளைவு தம்மை வெருவின) and turn that fear into austerity. The later fear is put to use, which limits the earlier counsel.

1553 shows treasure arriving and the king sunk in a sea of wealth (செல்வநீர்க் கடலுள் மூழ்கினான்), and Kural 332 gives wealth's coming and going as a crowd gathering and breaking up; the epic verse does not hint at loss, so the pairing is the couplet's general maxim laid beside a scene of plenty. 'Tests the image at its peak' adds nothing the verse says.

959 promises 'if trouble comes, think of me' (இடர்வரின் நினைக்க) and flies like lightning (மின்னெழூஉ); 15 has a god come 'like lightning' (மழை மின் என) to carry him from prison. The echo is real but 15 does not name the god or say he was called, and the 'debt owed for the mantra' is not in either verse.

Kuruntokai 174's woman says if he leaves for wealth, grace is nowhere (பொருளே மன்ற... அருளே); 1400 reports Civakan's saying that leaving for work and wealth is a man's duty (நினைத்து நீங்குதல் ஆண்கடன்). That much is a real contrast, but the epic does not quote the poem, and that the saying covers a secret departure comes only from the marker's hindsight, not from 1400.

1598 has wives 'living worshipping the husband's hands' (கணவற்கை தொழுது வாழ்வார்), close to Kural 55's கொழுநன் தொழுதெழுவாள், and gives their power as ending his distress, with no rain; the 'exception among many' depends on 1597, which is not in the packet. Real echo, thinly shown as a qualification.

1968 asks whether she knew him in an earlier birth (மேனாள் பிறந்தும் அறியுமோ), a question; Kuruntokai 40 asks how mothers, fathers and the two themselves were ever kin (எவ்வழி அறிதும்) and gives the union as rain in red earth. Nothing in the poem denies a former life, so 'tension' and 'the old poetry answered without any former life' overstate; the epic rather answers the poem's question.

1427 lists matted hair stretched out (சடை நீட்டல்), cloth and the skull bowl as seeds of a lowly birth (பீடிலாப் பிறவிக்கு வித்து), while Kural 280 says shaving and growing hair (மழித்தலும் நீட்டலும்) are not needed if one gives up what the world condemns. The epic goes from 'unneeded' to 'harmful', which is a true qualification.

200 calls the minister வெளிறு இலாக் கேள்வியான் and 385 has the teacher call him கல்லா மந்திரி; the two descriptions of one man conflict, and the second is rhetorical judgment after the crime. 'Learning counted by its fruit in conduct' is a fair reading and the Tamil supports the contrast.

1463 already says plainly that the discus killed its sender (தன்னையே செகுத்தது) alongside the curse simile, so the note's 'first a simile, then a plain statement' is not accurate; 1466 is the onlookers' restatement. It is a repeat of one event, not a development.

1520 has the kings bow in fear and 1530 has them hail him in the procession; this is plot sequence, and 'public kingship' is the proposer's gloss. Nothing in either verse reverses or fulfils the other.

Both lists share theft: 2870 gives theft's royal and next-birth punishments (களவு கடனாக கடிந்திடுதல் சூதே), 157 lists those who do not steal, drink or lie. 2870 is not a list of vows, and the speaker is Pavanamadevan to Asodharan, so 'a king who gives it to a son' is wrong; 'list of vows is a common form' is only a shared theme.

2607 has Vijayai ask the eight wives never to part (எங்கும் பிரியற்பீர்); 2987 has them decide on penance while still bound by love (காதல் நிகளத்தால்). Nothing in 2987 shows them parting from each other or from him, so the 'garlands parted' reading is built on the dream's meaning, not the Tamil, and no incompatible claim is stated.

396 gives the lord who has no taste of the senses (புலங்கிளர் பொறி நுகர்விலாத) opening doors that end hunger; Kural 225 ranks enduring hunger below removing it. Not tasting the senses is not the hunger-endurance the couplet ranks, so 'fills both places' stretches one term.

402 foretells that Kesava will take Ashvagriva's life and discus (தேசறு திகரியும் செவ்வன வெளவுமே); 114 says the palm lines mean the young lord will hold the discus weapon. Both are forecasts, so neither fulfils the other, and 114 does not call the prince Kesava, who is the 402 man by the note's assumption. 402's rival name is corrupt.

1760 says friends, wives and children can be gained but a brother cannot be made (உடன்பிறப்பாக்கலாகா); Kural 525 says giving and sweet speech gather layers of kin (சுற்றம்). The Kural does not limit its kin to an acquired circle, so 'the couplet gains a limit' is the proposer's, and the link is a loose topic match.

391 comforts Civakan and points to the living enemy (பகைவன் நின்றான்) and 392 shows his rage and the teacher stopping him: a consequence in plot order. 'The year of restraint' is not in either verse, and nothing here is incompatible with the other.

Both use the poor man's youth as the measure of a withered scene: 10 line 1 வறியவன் இளமை போல், 38 line 15 பொருள் இல்லான் இளமை போல் புல்லென்றாள். 38 moves it from the waste to the girl's face and pairs it with அருள் வல்லான் ஆக்கம், which poem 10 does not, and turns it into a challenge to marry.

The Silappathikaram unit names திருமா வளவன் but the Tamil does not fix him as Karikal Valavan of Purananuru 66, who is praised and then ranked below the Cheral who died of a back wound. The 'moral limit lost' comparison is the proposer's construction on a shared name.

165 has Urumannuvan promise a stratagem (உபாயத்தில் உடைப்பன்) and 166 shows the merchant disguise (வாணிக உருவினோடு) in the enemy camp; the later verse carries out the earlier plan. It is accurate but only a plan and its execution in plot order, with a thin lesson.

2051 only lists heaven's comforts and says nothing more can be said of them (சொன்மாடு பிறிதில்லை), and nothing there refers to householding or to Kural 50's 'placed among the gods'. The limit of the reward comes from 2060, not in the packet, so the pairing rests on a verse not shown.

2115 has the sword of meditation soaked in samadhi (தியானம் என்னும் கொற்றவாள்) cutting the enemy, and Tirumanthiram 121 has the Siva-yogi's bonds cut (துடக்கற) and the body as if dead. The two are not incompatible or even the same state: 121 names turiya, not samadhi, and its words are obscure. The 'opposite pictures' is a difference of image.

215 gives both a former-birth destiny (முனம் ஆகிய பான்மை) and the king's own heart (மனமாம் நெறி), and 475 only says he brought on his ruin by desire (முதற் கேடு சூழ்ந்த) without denying destiny. Silence is not a limit, so the two voices do not keep separate causes.

The shared token is the slipping bangles: Ainkurunuru 199 names him செறிவளை நெகிழ்த்தோன் and Kural 1157 says the bangles announce the leaving (தூற்றா). The poem does not say she climbs 'where all can see her' or claims the loss openly; 'exposure vs claiming it' is read in.

348 shows ascetic women meeting Vijayai and removing her ornaments; it says nothing of grief or of a widow's observances. Kannaki's lines in 18 ask whether she must 'waste away' like widows, but that is a different work, and 'opposite answers' with the son as the difference are the proposer's.

1157 only uses கச்சையங் களி நல் யானை as the king's epithet and says he burns in rage (கனன்று); Siddhar 2055 kills anger as a rutting elephant with the goad of reason (கோபமென்னும் மதயானை). Anger is not figured as an elephant in the epic, so the shared image is a coincidence of words.

2535 uses 'as people honour only the rich' (செல்வர்க்கே சிறப்புச் செய்யும்) and says the poor have no kin (நல்கூர்ந்தார்க்கில்லை சுற்றம்), which matches Kural 752's flat statement. The epic simply uses the maxim, not qualifying it, so 'agrees' fits better.

Both have the river play as war with syringes (சிவிறி): 966 has புறங்கண்டு, தவறு, திறை; Paripadal has போர் அணி and இகல். The convention is shared, but 'develops' implies a later completion not shown, and the 'terror at 973' is not in the packet. The sense of both is flagged uncertain.

1510 says the hero, hearing the list, was without swelling pride (வீங்கிய செருக்கிலன்) because those before were as many as sand, and Kural 979 calls greatness the absence of pride (பெருமிதம் இன்மை). The humility-from-numbers source is real, but line 2 is hard and the verse mostly illustrates the couplet.

Both say love shows in the eyes: Natrinai 23 has கண்ணே காமம் கரப்பு அரியவ்வே, Kural 1271 has கரப்பினும் கையிகந்து ஒல்லா உண்கண். The Natrinai does sort bangles and hair from the eyes, but 'supplies the test behind Valluvar's claim' assumes the Kural drew on it; the type is agrees, not develops.
